complexity.notes: Correct but slightly awkward structure: the elif chain pops the stack inside the condition, so a mismatched type pops an element and returns False anyway (harmless here, but fragile if extended). Using a dict mapping closers to openers (e.g. {')':'(', '}':'{', ']':'['}) plus a set for openers would be more idiomatic and concise.
complexity.summary: Classic stack-based validation: push opening brackets, and on each closing bracket pop and check the type matches; the string is valid iff the stack is empty at the end. Membership testing uses a small constant-size list, so each character is processed in O(1) time.
